title: Largest Number
prompt: Given a list of non-negative integers `nums`, arrange them so that they form the largest possible number when concatenated together, and return that number as a string. Since the result may be very large, it should be returned as a string rather than an integer.

examples.explanation: Arranging as "2" then "10" gives "210", which is larger than arranging "10" then "2" ("102").
When every number is zero, the naive concatenation would produce leading zeros like "00", so the result must collapse to a single "0".

hints: Sorting numerically or as plain strings both fail — you need a comparison rule specific to concatenation order.
For two numbers a and b (as strings), compare which concatenation is larger: a + b versus b + a.

Sort all numbers (as strings) using that pairwise comparator so that a should come before b whenever a + b > b + a. Concatenate in that sorted order, and handle the all-zero edge case where the result would have leading zeros.

solution.approach: Convert every number to a string, then sort the strings with a custom comparator: string a should be placed before string b exactly when the concatenation a + b is lexicographically greater than b + a. This comparator is a valid total order for this purpose because it directly compares the two possible local orderings of any pair, and that pairwise-optimal choice composes into a globally optimal arrangement (this is the standard argument for exchange-based greedy proofs). After sorting, concatenate all strings; special-case the result being all zeros (e.g. input [0,0]) by returning "0" instead of "000".
